name: vydeo-mcp

tools.name: vydeo_connect
tools.description: Connect this Claude to the user's vydeo account. Opens vydeo in their browser to approve, shows them a short code to check, and saves the connection on this computer. Run it first, and again if any tool says the connection is no longer valid.

tools.name: vydeo_status
tools.description: Check the vydeo connection, the account email, the plan and the credits left. Members are paid plans only. If the account has no plan, this returns the plans and where to buy one.

tools.name: vydeo_disconnect
tools.description: Forget the vydeo connection on this computer. Only run it when the user asks to disconnect.

tools.name: vydeo_setup
tools.description: One-time preparation of the editing studio, which Claude uses to look at the edit while designing it. Tell the user it is a one-time download of about 150 MB and may take a few minutes. Other tools run it automatically if it has not been done.

tools.name: vydeo_list_styles
tools.description: List the edit styles vydeo offers. Show them to the user and let them choose one before you design an edit.

tools.name: vydeo_get_style
tools.description: Get the full direction for one style: what it looks like, how it paces and which music it uses. Read it before designing, and compare your preview frames against it afterwards.

tools.name: vydeo_get_playbook
tools.description: Get vydeo's rules for directing an edit: how to place components on the timeline, the component reference and the valid sound effect names. Read it before you design or change a timeline and follow it exactly.

tools.name: vydeo_import_footage
tools.description: Upload the user's talking-head video from this computer to vydeo. vydeo cuts and transcribes it and creates a draft you can edit. This can take a few minutes for a long file. Returns the draft id, its revision and the editor link. Give the user the editor link so they can watch the draft and export the finished video from there.

path.description: Full path to the video file on this computer.

title.description: A short name for the draft.

tools.name: vydeo_add_media
tools.description: Upload a local b-roll clip, photo, logo or music file to a draft. It becomes an asset you can reference in the timeline as "media:<asset_id>" (b-roll and graphics) or in a music clip. Returns the asset and the new revision.

path.description: Full path to the file on this computer.

role.description: music for a music bed, media for anything else.

label.description: A short name, such as "Product shot".

tools.name: vydeo_add_style_music
tools.description: Use this after choosing a style whose music is set (see vydeo_get_style). It adds the style's own music bed under the voice, ducked, along the whole timeline, so read the timeline again afterwards. Adding the same style twice changes nothing. Returns the asset and the new revision.

tools.name: vydeo_list_drafts
tools.description: List the user's drafts, newest first, with their revision and editor link.

tools.name: vydeo_get_timeline
tools.description: Read a draft's timeline and its current revision. Always read before changing a draft, because the user may have edited it in the editor. Spoken words are left out unless include_words is true, to save space.

tools.name: vydeo_update_timeline
tools.description: Save changes to a draft as a new revision that shows up live in the vydeo editor. Send only the parts that change: each key you send in changes (layout, frame, duration_seconds, footage_end, footage, words, captions, broll, graphics, music, sfx) replaces that whole field, so send the full list for it. base_revision is the revision you last read. If the draft moved on, read it again and reapply your change. If the timeline is rejected the reply lists what to fix. Give the user the editor link so they can watch the draft and export the finished video from there.

summary.description: One plain sentence on what changed, shown to the user in the editor.

tools.name: vydeo_preview_frames
tools.description: Render still frames of the draft at the given times (1 to 6 seconds on the edited timeline) so you can see your own work. Check the hook, every graphic and the end card, compare with the style guidance and fix what looks wrong. Runs the editing studio on this computer, so it is slower the first time.

tools.name: vydeo_open_editor
tools.description: Open a draft in the vydeo editor in the user's browser. The finished video is exported from there.

instructions:
vydeo edits short vertical videos. You do the creative work here and the user watches it appear live in the vydeo editor. This server never renders or saves a final video file. The finished video is exported from the vydeo editor, so if the user asks for the file, send them to the editor link.

First use: run vydeo_connect (the user approves in their browser), then vydeo_setup once.

Magic Edit, where the user picks a style and you build the whole edit:
1. vydeo_import_footage with the user's take, or use an existing draft from vydeo_list_drafts.
2. vydeo_list_styles, then let the user choose one.
3. vydeo_get_style for that style. If it has music, call vydeo_add_style_music before designing, so the music clip is already in the timeline you read. Then vydeo_get_playbook, and design the timeline by the playbook's rules.
4. vydeo_update_timeline to save it.
5. vydeo_preview_frames at the key moments: the hook, every graphic and the end card. Compare what you see with the style guidance, fix what looks wrong with another update, and repeat until nothing is left to improve.
6. Always give the user the editor link so they can watch and export.

Live editing, where the user describes changes as they go: vydeo_get_timeline, apply exactly what was asked as one vydeo_update_timeline with a clear one-sentence summary, then confirm the change is visible in the editor. Keep the base_revision from the last read, and read again after a conflict.

Paid plans only: if a tool says a plan is needed, show the user the plans and the link it gives, then run the tool again once they have picked one.
